scenes.text: In 1971 the dollar stopped being tied to gold. Here is what an ounce has cost since.
August 1971: Nixon closes the gold window. The official price is thirty-five dollars.
January 1980: with inflation raging, gold is fixed at eight hundred and fifty dollars.
By 1999 central banks are selling, and gold sinks to about two hundred and fifty.
In 2011 debt-crisis fears push it to a record near nineteen hundred.
And in August 2020, pandemic stimulus sends it past two thousand. About fifty-nine times 1971.

props.title: Gold after the dollar left it
props.takeaway: Same ounce, about *59 times* the 1971 price.
